keyFindings.text: **"Session resume" is artifact resume only, and the code models it for half the kinds.** No builder forwards a resume or session flag: claude runs `-p`, codex runs `exec`, opencode runs `run --standalone`, and the four other builders do the same without a session argument. `EXECUTOR_SESSION_ENV_BY_KIND` names a session env for codex, claude, opencode and cursor and deliberately omits pi, vibe and dsh; `EXECUTOR_STATE_ENV_BY_KIND` names a state dir for every kind. For dsh the gap is structural: one fresh `DSH_HOME` is created per attempt and removed when the attempt settles, so a retry cannot resume the previous attempt's harness state even if a resume flag existed. keyFindings.text: **A depth band's spend is summed across all its nodes, so one node's revisits can close its siblings.** `applyBandBudget` accumulates `spent[band] += visits[index].spent` and, once that sum reaches `cap * share`, closes every open node in the band as `exhausted/budget`. There is no per-node floor, so a three-node depth-1 band with a 5-visit allotment closes all three as soon as the run has made five visits across them, even if one node got four of those visits and another got one. In the previous run this is how F-1-006 closed after a single pass on it. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:360] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:386] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2556]

**Cross-lineage duplicate questions are invisible to admission and to the merge guard.** Each lineage receives only its own share of the node store, and `step_frontier_admit` builds `known-texts` from that lineage's registry, rejected patterns and exhausted list. `checkProposal` therefore compares a proposal with its own store and its own known texts, never with a sibling lineage's questions; the merge guard checks node ids, not question text. A re-worded version of another lineage's question passes both, which is the mechanism behind the previous run's unbudgeted duplicate work after a frontier drained. Passing a root-level question-digest file (dedupe keys for every dealt node and every answered question) into each lineage's admission closes it without a new service. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/fanout-run.cjs:423] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:755] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:763]

**Depth bands are enforced only in the reducer projection, never at admission.** The node cap is band-blind: `maxFrontierNodes` counts live nodes at every depth, and `maxChildrenPerNode` bounds one parent, but nothing stops all growth slots from landing at depth 2. A depth-2 band of 3.5 visits then has to cover every depth-2 node the run admitted, while depth-1 nodes are still open and will later demand their own band. Reserving a band's growth slots at admission (`floor(bandShare / minimumPassesPerNode)`, minus the nodes already at that depth) would make the split an admission rule instead of a post-hoc close. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:438] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:771] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-research/scripts/reduce-state.cjs:2673]

**Growth slots are one run-wide number, filled in delta order, so the first node worked can spend the whole frontier's growth.** `seedBudget` computes `growthSlots = nodeCap - seeded` (2 for a 3-seed, 10-iteration lineage), and `checkProposal` prunes on `countLiveNodes >= maxFrontierNodes` regardless of which parent is asking. `admitProposals` then walks the delta's rows in order. This run shows it live: F-1-002's two proposals filled the cap at iteration 1, and this node's FRONTIER block now prints "This node has no child slots left, so do not propose children" while F-1-004 and F-1-006 have never been worked. A deterministic spread — sort proposals by parent depth, then by fewest live children, before admission — would stop one node from taking the run's whole growth budget. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:515] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:778] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs:828]

**The four held rows have a dependency order: 30 + 12 as one change, then 13 with the adapter capability test, then 29 last.** Row 12 (one `projectFrontier`) is the shared parser and projection; row 30 (per-node research dashboard) is the renderer that consumes it, and the backlog already pairs them. Row 13 (one executor path) is independent of the frontier work but needs row 2's permission fix (delivered) and the capability manifest from F-1-002 to keep the merged path honest; doing it before 29 also removes the hand-built branches that make some aliases look live. Row 29 deletes config-key aliases, legacy migration and binary probes; it is safest after 12 and 13, because those two changes decide which keys and probes have no caller. Building 29 first would delete aliases whose only remaining reader is a branch that 13 has not yet collapsed. **An iteration with findings but no answered question writes zero graph evidence, so the evidence guards pass by having nothing to inspect.** `readResearchIterationEvidence` reads the delta's finding rows, but `deriveResearchFindingEvidence` runs only when `evidence.answeredQuestions.length > 0`. Iteration 1 of this run had seven cited findings and produced `insertedNodes: 0`; the stop decision then reported `nodeCount: 0` and marked `sourceDiversity` and `singleWeakSource` as `notEvaluated`, which counts as a pass. Iteration 2 answered a question and the same command inserted 9 nodes and 21 edges, so the switch is the answered-question guard, not a malformed delta. Attaching findings to the active frontier node when no question is answered, or reporting the guards as `insufficient` rather than `passed`, would stop the false green. **Every iteration record produces a "Trusted evidence yield was absent" warning because the leaf contract does not carry the field the ledger schema requires.** `legacy-compatibility.ts` converts a contract-shaped iteration record into the ledger shape, sets `trustedEvidenceYield: 0`, and pushes the warning; the field is required as a ratio in the schema, yet the prompt pack's record example does not list it. This run's gateway receipts carried the warning on both iterations. Either the prompt pack adds a runner-computable yield (for example distinct cited sources per finding, capped at 1) or the compatibility layer derives it silently from `findingsCount` and cited sources. A warning that fires on every correct record trains the operator to ignore warnings. **The `structured_state_findings_partially_reflected_in_registry` alarm fires on a legitimate refinement.** The reducer folds a row that names `refines: <earlier id>` into that earlier entry and records a `Refinement of an earlier finding` transition, so the registry deliberately holds fewer entries than the iteration rows. `synthesis-closeout.cjs` then counts distinct iteration ids against distinct registry ids and raises the alarm when the registry count is lower. Any run that refines a finding therefore reports "synthesis incomplete" while the registry is correct. Storing the folded ids on the target (`refinedFrom`) and counting them in `registryEvidence` would make the two counts agree without weakening the invariant. **The closeout scopes a research synthesis row to `parentSessionId`, while the run's own iteration rows are scoped to `sessionId`.** `runScope` sets `lineageId = lineage.parentSessionId` (falling back to `runId`) for research and puts it in the event stem's scope. One config-owned `lineageId` (written by init and read by both the leaf record and the closeout) removes the inference. **The conformance test is four fixture assertions over `buildLineageCommand`, one per divergence that is currently undetected.** (a) Given a fixed lineage and a prompt, exactly one channel carries it: one `promptArgIndexes` entry, or `input === prompt` with a trailing `-`, or a `--prompt-file` path; `redactedArgs` must show one digest. (c) A synthetic log fixture per `costSource` must make `sumProviderCostFromLog` return the declared shape or null, so a null is labelled rather than anonymous. Self-invocation is still refused for the others by the stack, ancestry or lockfile layers, but the coverage is implicit in code rather than stated per kind. A guard-layer row beside the adapter capability record would make "this kind cannot self-detect by env" a declared fact instead of a comment. **The honest fix is to name artifact resume, and to capture a provider id only if model-session resume is actually wanted.** Today's behaviour is coherent: a rerun resumes the loop from `deep-research-state.jsonl` and the node store, which is what makes a retry cheap. Calling it "session resume" overstates it. If provider resume is wanted, the JSON shapes already carry an id (opencode's events and cursor's `--output-format json` both report one), so the runner can extract it, persist it in the lineage config under a `providerSession` key, and pass the adapter's resume flag on a rerun; until then, the capability record should say `resume: artifact-only` for every kind. **The only rerun identity is the stored SPECKIT session id, and no adapter turns it into a provider-session resume.** `buildLineageDispatch` calls `readStoredLineageSessionId` and falls back to `fanout-<label>-<runId>`; the id is written into the prompt and the preview as `session_id`. No builder emits `--resume`, `--session`, `--continue` or a codex `exec resume` subcommand, and the runner does not parse a `session_id` out of a CLI log. A `--only-lineage` rerun therefore re-reads the lineage's artifacts and prompt but starts a fresh provider conversation. ruledOutDirections.text: **Adding a new mirror-drift checker.** Both existing gates pass at HEAD, and the crosswalk documents the absent command trees as sanctioned. Building another checker adds a second source of truth for a surface that is already green.

**Reading `--output-format json` support from the CLI help only.** The adapters are already pinned to live-verified flags in comments; a help probe would not prove the runner reads the resulting log shape, which is the actual gap.

**Treating the stress matrix as already conformant because it names all 14 rows.** The names exist, but the rows do not include the four differences this iteration found, and the non-codex cells are declared pending.

Grepping `fanout-run.cjs` for a per-kind session-id capture that could feed a rerun: only `readStoredLineageSessionId`, which reads the lineage's own config, exists. No provider session id is stored for a retry.
Looking for a shared `resolveSandboxMode` in the single-executor branches: each branch computes its own, which is the root of Finding 1.

**A larger run-wide node cap as the fix for "5 of 7 pruned".** Raising the cap spends more iterations on the same first-worked branch; the pruned questions were good, but the run had no budget to work them. The defect is allocation, not the number.

**Building row 12 alone and leaving the dashboard for later.** The dashboard is the surface that would have shown the band closes and the partition drift; splitting it from the shared projection leaves the operator with the same blind spot.

**Ranking proposals by model-written value or confidence.** The runner cannot audit a self-asserted score, which is the honesty problem this packet is about. Sorting by parent depth and live-child count is deterministic and checkable.
Looking for a cross-lineage question comparison in `fanout-merge.cjs`: the partition guard compares node ids only, so question overlap has no check anywhere.
Looking for a per-band cap in `readCaps`: only `maxDepth`, `maxChildrenPerNode`, `maxRootChildren` and `maxFrontierNodes` exist. Band shares are consumed by the reducer, never by admission.

**Deleting the `structured_state_findings_partially_reflected_in_registry` invariant.** The invariant is right that a count mismatch matters; the defect is that the count ignores a documented refinement transition. Deleting the check would hide a real loss.
**Fixing the commit step by adding the ignored path to `.gitignore` again.** It is already there; the exclude is the redundant half.

**Treating the `Trusted evidence yield` line as a harmless informational message.** It is emitted only on the legacy-compatibility path, which is the path every CLI lineage takes; leaving it names a missing field as a permanent warning.
Looking for a `lineageId` field in this lineage's config: only `sessionId` and `parentSessionId` exist, so the closeout has to infer one.
Searching for refinement handling in `synthesis-closeout.cjs`: there is none, which is the finding. The reducer owns the concept and the closeout does not read it.
**Deriving the contract from the CLI help text at test time.** The adapters are pinned to live-verified flags, and a help probe cannot prove the runner reads the log shape the flag produces.
**One test per adapter kind written by hand.** That is the current `expectSuccessArgs` shape; it duplicates the builder and drifts with it.
**Treating the contract as documentation only.** The point is that the builder and the test read one table; a prose table with no consumer is another document to rot.
Looking for a capability record already shipped under another name: `EXECUTOR_KIND_FLAG_SUPPORT` is the closest, and it answers "is the field accepted", not "how is it carried".
**Adding another CI workflow for the validator.** The existing deep-loop workflow already installs and runs the suite; one added step is enough.
**Rewriting the validator to import the tests instead of listing them.** `vitest list` is the supported discovery surface; the parser, not the mechanism, is wrong.
**Treating `CLI_ADAPTER_STRESS_MATRIX` as the live matrix.** The overlay is the live object and the audit proves it; the seed table is documentation of the phase-one state.
Grepping workflows for `cli-adapter` or `validate-playbook-package`: only the sk-doc validator appears, which is a different path and a different package.

**Adding resume flags to all eight adapters at once.** Four kinds report no session id in a parseable shape, and the two unconfirmed envs would need live probes; per-kind capture is the only honest path.

**Persisting the env value as the rerun identity.** The env is the parent's provider session, not the child's, and the recursion guard deliberately reads it to refuse dispatch; storing it would conflate the guard with resume.
**Treating `session_id` in the preview as a provider id.** It is the SPECKIT session used for artifact scoping, as `buildLineageDispatch` shows.
Grepping for `--resume` or `exec resume` in `fanout-run.cjs` and `dispatch-iteration.cjs`: no match. The absence is the finding.
Looking for a log parser that extracts a session id: none exists; the only log parsers are cost and quota.
